# Rhys Hume

> Rhys Hume is a developer based in Glasgow. He builds websites, custom business software and automations for engineering firms and small businesses, and validates computerised systems for regulated manufacturers. Engineering and fabrication firms are his specialist market, and he also works with other small businesses. Customers deal with him directly. He comes from a computer system validation background.

## The idea

Websites that help a business win work, and systems and automations that help it manage the work: a site that is easy to find and takes the quote request, automation that drafts quotes for a person to approve and chases them, job management in Tolra (in pilot), and computer system validation for regulated manufacturers underneath. AI is used where it helps and a person approves anything that goes out.

## Services

- [Websites for engineering firms](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/engineering): the website, quote workflow and job management for fabrication and machining firms, so enquiries, quotes and jobs stop getting lost between emails and spreadsheets. Tolra is in pilot with a Glasgow shop
- [Websites](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/websites): mobile-friendly websites with quote request forms, set up for local search, for engineering and manufacturing firms. A free website preview is available at https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/contact: a first look at what a site could look like, not a finished website
- [Websites for small businesses](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/local-business): websites, care plans, filming, Google search set up, online listings and structured data, automation and AI set up, and domain and email set up for small businesses in Glasgow and Central Scotland, with from prices and a written quote. Includes the website from £1,500, the website with quote workflow from £3,800, and care plans from £35 a month
- [Automation](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/automation): automation and custom software for admin problems such as enquiries that need preparing for quotes, the same details typed into different systems, and job information spread across spreadsheets, delivered around the tools a business already uses as a short pilot on one process, with optional monthly care afterwards. It explains when plain automation, AI or a custom system fits best
- [Tolra](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/tolra): job management for small CNC and fabrication shops, in pilot
- [Computer system validation](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/csv): validation plans, risk assessments, IQ/OQ/PQ protocols, traceability, data migration, validation reports and periodic review for regulated manufacturers. "I work to GAMP® 5 Second Edition, EU Annex 11 and 21 CFR Part 11 principles"

## Work and more

- [JNR Engineering case study](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/work/jnr-engineering): the website and the systems behind it for a machining and fabrication firm in Hamilton (a family firm), with no measured results claimed
- [Council digital grants](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/council-digital-grants): a detailed project quote to support a council digital grant application in East Dunbartonshire or North Lanarkshire
- [Insights](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/insights): practical notes for engineering firms, starting with [what to put on an engineering firm's website to win more RFQs](https://www.rhyshume.co.uk/insights/what-to-put-on-an-engineering-firms-website)
